sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite binary-path support \(\mathcal S\), rational probability floor \(\epsilon\), and positive ex ante reshaping law. The inverse analysis ranges over the entire compact floor domain and uses the probability-vector polynomial graph, so all pair-product compatibility constraints are retained. Absorption is required only for the ordered Green, graph-rank, and adjacent-ratio corollaries. In the separate published layer, taking \(\mathcal S=\mathcal S^*\) reproduces the published support exactly.
sampling_model.units: Population identification uses i.i.d. triples \((X_i,W_i,Y_i)\) from \(P\). This base superpopulation layer is not the published class and is incomparable with it. A separate theorem uses the published possibly dependent, non-identically distributed unit-indexed triangular array and its maximal-correlation condition, so homogeneous recovery is direct in that layer rather than transferred from the base class.
sampling_model.treatment: In the base algebra, \(W_i\) may be any path in the declared finite binary support. The published layer uses its arbitrary binary-path support \(\mathcal S^*\). Ordered adoption-time results explicitly restrict support to absorbing paths.
sampling_model.overlap: The population layer assumes \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\) and \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\). The published layer instead uses known unit-specific propensities \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_*\) on the reshaping support and defines its RIPW weight to be zero off that support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population functional uses a correct common generalized path propensity and pathwise conditional means. The anchor-faithful statistical theorem is for the published known-propensity estimator and yields the \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\) coefficient approximation; it does not assert cross-fitted or doubly robust inference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under their unit-indexed known-propensity setup, Assumptions 2.1--2.3, a calendar-homogeneous finite-lag outcome model, and a nonsingular reshaped design, each dynamic RIPW coefficient converges to the corresponding average lag effect. The present theorem works in exactly that layer upon taking the reshaping support to be their \(\mathcal S^*\), extends the coefficient approximation to calendar-varying effects at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and shows by a block construction that no uniformly faster rate follows from those conditions alone.
A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

body.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, the paper identifies the reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient as an exact linear functional of calendar-specific current and carryover effects and gives support-only rank and exact forward diagnostics. On the full-rank probability-floor domain, the complete loading image is a compact semialgebraic body. A terminating exact real-algebraic procedure decides target membership and returns either an algebraic feasible law or an attained closest loading, a metric-separation certificate, and exact worst-case contamination over coordinatewise bounded effects; generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition is potentially doubly exponential. The separate published unit-indexed layer retains the tensor approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), with a block witness showing that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from its stated conditions. The remaining open problem is a support-uniform ordered/combinatorial description of chamber counts, signs, incidences, and simultaneous off-diagonal-zero strata, not finite-instance decidability.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory establishes dynamic consistency under calendar-homogeneous effects and leaves its calendar-varying DATE equation beyond scope. Its class and the base i.i.d. conditional-mean layer remain incomparable. Existing event-study decompositions and supplied-law numerical diagnostics do not provide the complete finite-memory calendar-by-lag loading body, exact inverse membership, certified closest loading, or exact bounded-effect contamination on an arbitrary listed support.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are an arbitrary-path loading tensor shared algebraically across two explicitly separated sampling layers and an exact finite-instance inverse analysis that respects probability-product compatibility on every exceptional stratum. Ordered absorption structure remains useful for a sharper structural chamber law, but is not needed for exact decidability.
project_justification.fill: The project proves arbitrary-path covariance and pair-mass identities, exact normalization, rational supplied-law diagnostics, and the positive-law support-rank law. It encodes the complete full-rank probability-floor loading body by its polynomial probability-vector graph, proves compact semialgebraicity and uniform invertibility, and uses exact real-algebraic elimination to return membership witnesses or an attained closest loading with a metric-separation certificate and exact bounded-effect worst-case contamination. The generic algorithm terminates but may be doubly exponential and does not replace the open ordered/combinatorial chamber classification. In the separate published triangular-array layer, the calendar-varying tensor approximation remains \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and the block construction rules out any uniformly faster rate from the stated conditions alone.

body.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary binary-path support, unit-specific known generalized propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, non-identical units, and weak cross-unit dependence. The base i.i.d. conditional-mean class is not their published class and is incomparable with it. The separate unit-indexed theorem retains their class exactly upon taking the reshaping support to be \(\mathcal S^*\), extends the coefficient approximation to calendar-varying finite-memory effects at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and directly recovers their homogeneous theorem; its block construction shows that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from their stated conditions alone. Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients but do not analyze assignment-law reshaping or its complete inverse image. Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) motivate treatment-history indexing under known experimental assignment, while de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) study time-constant random-coefficient distributed lags. Wright (2026) supplies adjacent numerical diagnostic evidence and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) supply time-varying distributed-lag modeling precedent; none supplies the present exact probability-graph loading body, membership or metric-separation certificate, and closest-loading bounded-effect contamination calculation. Collins (1975) supplies the standard generic cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition algorithm; the contribution here is the exact loading-tensor encoding and certified inverse analysis, not generic quantifier elimination itself.
body.honest_scope: The forward tensor algebra and exact loading-body inverse procedure cover arbitrary finite binary-path supports. In the nonsingular support branch the probability floor yields uniform invertibility, compactness, attainment, and exact real-algebraic membership or metric-separation certificates; feasible and optimizing laws may be algebraic rather than rational. The closest loading uses the declared tensor \(\ell_1\) diagnostic, and bounded-effect contamination is minimized secondarily only among its minimizers. Generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition is exact and terminating but potentially doubly exponential; no convexity, linear separating hyperplane, polynomial-time method, or closed support-uniform structural chamber law is claimed. The ordered/combinatorial enumeration of chamber counts, loading signs, boundary incidences, and simultaneous off-diagonal-zero strata remains open. The separate published triangular-array theorem proves the coefficient approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\) and shows that no uniformly faster rate follows from the stated conditions. No central limit theorem, asymptotic normality, cross-fitted robust inference, or empirical application is supplied.
